intro.title: Build image resize endpoint pipeline
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Node.js endpoint that receives an image, resizes it to a specified width and height, and returns the processed image. You'll learn how to handle file uploads using the `multer` middleware, manipulate images with the `sharp` library, and stream the result back in a response. The core concept is creating a pipeline that processes data through sequential steps: receiving, transforming, and outputting. By the end, you'll have a functional API endpoint that can dynamically resize images on demand.
intro.usecase: Image resizing endpoints are essential in modern web applications that handle user-generated content, such as social media platforms like Instagram or Facebook. When users upload profile pictures or share photos, these services automatically create multiple optimized versions for different display contexts—thumbnails, feeds, and high-resolution views. E-commerce sites like Amazon use similar pipelines to generate product image variants for listings, galleries, and mobile previews. Developers implement these endpoints to ensure fast loading times, consistent visual quality, and efficient storage across diverse device screens and bandwidth conditions.
